lemonde.description: Les mesures de lutte contre le réchauffement ne sont pas de simples ajustements techniques. Or sur les politiques menées pour ralentir ou entraver la poursuite du réchauffement, les critiques de l’action conduite depuis dix ans s’accumulent, observe Stéphane Foucart, journaliste au service « Planète », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.description: L’avion, qui s’est écrasé à Tomblaine, transportait un groupe de personnes pour un baptême de parachutisme. Les victimes sont cinq moniteurs, cinq élèves et le pilote ; « il n’y a pas de victimes collatérales », selon le préfet. Le ministre de l’intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, est attendu sur place.

lemonde.description: La phase de groupes de la plus grande Coupe du monde de l’histoire, du moins par ses dimensions, s’est achevée samedi 27 juin. De la Côte ouest à la Côte est des Etats-Unis, en passant par Mexico et Vancouver, les cinq envoyés spéciaux du « Monde » dressent son bilan.

lemonde.title: Vladimir Poutine ou la solitude de l’« Homo sovieticus »
lemonde.description: Entre déni de réalité, désir de revanche et communication calibrée, le président russe tente de se poser en maître du jeu. Mais, après plus de quatre ans de guerre en Ukraine, ces vieilles ficelles héritées du passé soviétique montrent leurs limites, et l’homme fort du Kremlin est en perte de crédibilité.

france24fr.title: Cuba se tourne vers l'énergie solaire face au blocus énergétique des États-Unis
france24fr.description: Depuis que Washington impose un blocus pétrolier de facto à la Havane, l'île vit au rythme des coupures de courant. Les habitants se tournent vers de nouvelles solutions, dont l'énergie solaire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Coupe du monde suivie à Gaza
france24fr.description: À Gaza, les matchs de la Coupe du monde sont diffusés dans des cafés improvisés. Une parenthèse dans un quotidien éprouvant.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : des sauveteurs du monde entier arrivent au Venezuela
france24fr.description: Le temps presse pour retrouver des survivants plus de 72 heures après le double séisme au Venezuela dont le bilan continue de s'alourdir. Des secouristes du monde entier viennent en aide à la population, rapporte notre correspondante Alice Campaignolle.

france24fr.title: États-Unis et Iran poursuivent leurs bombardements et s'accusent mutuellement
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis et l'Iran poursuivent leurs bombardements dans le ⁠Golfe, chacun accusant ​l'autre de violer un protocole d'accord de plus en plus précaire, signé il y a moins de deux semaines et censé mettre fin à près de ​quatre mois de conflit entre les deux pays.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : arbitrage, pauses fraîcheur, pelouse... les tops et les flops de la phase de groupes
france24fr.description: La phase de groupes du Mondial 2026 a pris fin dimanche après presque trois semaines de compétition. À mi-parcours, cette Coupe du monde nouveau format donne à voir du bon et du moins bon : les arbitres qui laissent beaucoup plus jouer, les pauses fraîcheurs... France 24 fait ses tops et ses flops à l'issue des 72 premiers matches de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Nouvelle-Calédonie : les électeurs aux urnes pour un scrutin décisif
france24fr.description: Les Calédoniens ont commencé à voter dimanche 28 juin pour les premières élections provinciales depuis 2019, un scrutin qui doit redessiner les rapports de force politiques de l'archipel et peser sur les négociations à venir sur son avenir institutionnel, dans l'impasse depuis les émeutes de 2024. Nous en parlons avec notre envoyé spécial Karim Yahiaoui.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : début des 16es de finale ce soir
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle phase débute dans cette Coupe du monde de football : celle des 16es de finale. Ce soir, première rencontre entre l'Afrique du Sud et le Canada. Nous revenons sur les moments forts de cette phase de poules avec notre envoyé spécial Cédric Ferreira.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la Colombie termine devant des Portugais décevants
france24fr.description: Le Portugal devait battre la Colombie pour récupérer la première place du groupe K. Mais c’est la Colombie qui était la plus proche de l’emporter. Les deux équipes se sont finalement quittées sur un score nul.

france24fr.title: Canicule : les craintes se confirment sur de nombreux décès en France
france24fr.description: Des morts qui se mesurent déjà en centaines, et probablement en milliers. Les premiers chiffres officiels commencent à remonter dimanche sur les effets de la canicule exceptionnelle qui s'achève en France mais dont les conséquences sur l'organisme vont encore durer des jours.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : 72 heures après les séismes meurtriers, la quête de survivants continue
france24fr.description: Le temps presse pour retrouver des survivants 72 heures après le double séisme au Venezuela dont le bilan continue de s'alourdir : 1 430 morts et plus de 50 000 disparus, alors que l'aide humanitaire internationale monte en puissance sur place.

france24fr.title: L'Iran cible le Koweït et Bahreïn après des frappes américaines sur son sol
france24fr.description: L'Iran s'est affirmé dimanche "déterminé" à défendre sa souveraineté et a mené des frappes visant le Koweït et Bahreïn, au lendemain d'attaques américaines contre son territoire, un regain de tension qui menace la poursuite des négociations pour mettre un terme au conflit au Moyen-Orient.

france24fr.title: "C'est notre hémisphère" : la Colombie étend la zone d'influence de Trump en Amérique latine
france24fr.description: La victoire d’Abelardo De La Espriella à la présidentielle en Colombie offre un nouvel allié à la Maison Blanche, qui entend "restaurer sa prééminence dans l’hémisphère occidental". Au total, on dénombre 12 pays latino-américains dont les gouvernements sont proches de Washington, qui lorgne désormais le Brésil et Cuba.

france24fr.title: En Nouvelle-Calédonie, un vote dans le calme pour des élections provinciales à hauts enjeux
france24fr.description: Les Calédoniens se sont rendus aux urnes ce dimanche dans le cadre d'élections provinciales aux enjeux majeurs. Il s'agit du premier scrutin provincial depuis 2019.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : la quête éperdue de survivants trois jours après les séismes meurtriers
france24fr.description: Le temps presse pour retrouver des survivants plus de 72 heures après le double séisme au Venezuela dont le bilan continue de s'alourdir : 1 430 morts et plus de 50 000 disparus. Les habitants de La Guaira, zone la plus affectée par la catastrophe, tentent de dégager les victimes avec des moyens très rudimentaires.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Canicule en direct : environ 1 000 décès supplémentaires que la normale recensés en France
Canicule en direct : plus de 1 300 décès imputables à la vague de chaleur en Europe, selon l'OMS
france24fr.description: Depuis mercredi, un millier de décès de plus que la normale ont été recensés en France, a annoncé dimanche l'Agence nationale de santé publique, alors que s'achève une canicule exceptionnelle par son intensité. L'agence a prévenu que le bilan réel est voué à s'alourdir. L'OMS évalue pour sa part le nombre de morts imputables à la vague de chaleur en Europe à plus de 1 300. Suivez notre direct.

zeit.description: Zu Beginn ihres Wahlkampfs für die Landtagswahlen kritisieren die Grünen die Bundesregierung heftig. Diese »belehre und beschimpfe« die Bevölkerung.

zeit.description: Für christliche Fußballer gibt es jetzt göttliche Accessoires.

nzz.description: Die Privatmaschine ist offenbar kurz nach dem Start bei Nancy abgestürzt.

nzz.description: Nach eineinhalb Jahren regierungskritischer Proteste sollen in Serbien vorgezogene Präsidentschafts- und Parlamentswahlen stattfinden. Dahinter steckt ein taktisches Manöver Vucics, um weiterhin an der Macht zu bleiben.

nzz.description: Nach dem 3:3 ziehen Österreich und Algerien in den Sechzehntelfinal ein – die Algerier mit dem Nationalcoach Vladimir Petkovic treffen dort auf die Schweiz.

nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar vereinbarten die beiden Länder Mitte Juni eine Waffenruhe. Doch diese ist fragil. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.description: Drei Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf Mensch und Umwelt? Hier finden Sie die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: Im Donbass rückt Russland weiter vor – trotz den ukrainischen Angriffen aufs Hinterland
nzz.description: Mit Kostjantiniwka steht die südlichste Stadt des ukrainischen Festungsrings vor dem Fall. Im Donbass sind die Folgen der intensivierten ukrainischen Drohnenangriffe auf Russland bis anhin nicht zu spüren.

nzz.title: Schwedisches Romandebüt: Ist Heimat ein Ort oder ein Gefühl?
nzz.description: Die Schwedin Sanna Samuelsson sucht nach ihrer verlorenen Kindheit auf dem Bauernhof, der kein Bullerbü ist. Ihr Debütroman ist poetisch und derb zugleich.

nzz.title: Papa, wann stirbst du endlich? Nefeli Kavouras' Familienroman über letzte Dinge
nzz.description: Nefeli Kavouras schreibt leichtfüssig und mit einer erstaunlichen Wendung über einen Abschied. Ein lesenswerter Debütroman.

nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: Der Bundesrat hat es gerade gut. Doch ist das auch gut für unser Land?
nzz.description: Die Landesregierung regiert für einmal erstaunlich harmonisch und ohne dass sich die Bundesräte zu sehr ins jeweilige Gärtchen treten. Doch die Entscheide, die daraus resultieren, lösen trotzdem harsche Kritik aus.

nzz.title: Korruption und Misswirtschaft rächen sich nun beim Erdbeben in Venezuela
nzz.description: Das Regime sperrt den Zugang zur Katastrophenprovinz La Guaira. Offiziell, um die Bergungsarbeiten zu erleichtern. Doch es geht auch um die Verschleierung der Bausünden und der inkompetenten Verwaltung.

observador.title: Zizou Bergs vence torneio de ténis de Eastbourne
observador.description: O atual 48.º classificado do ranking tinha perdido as duas finais anteriormente disputadas, ambas no ano passado, nomeadamente em 's-Hertogenbosch, também em relva.

observador.title: Alverca oficializa saída do treinador Custódio Castro
observador.description: Custódio Castro assumiu a equipa no início da época passada, guiando os alverquenses ao 11.º lugar da I Liga e à desejada manutenção no primeiro escalão um ano após a subida.

observador.title: 13h. Venezuela. Número de portugueses mortos sobe para 51
observador.description: São 44 lusodescendentes, 6 portugueses (nacionais) e 1 português por casamento. Ainda, o Papa Leão 14 agradece a todos os que têm ajudado a Venezuela depois dos sismos desta semana.

observador.title: Sismos. Oposição na Venezuela denuncia proibições de ajudar
observador.description: Oposição diz-se proibida de usar termo "centro de doação". Há vídeos que mostram polícia a desmobilizar recolhas. Especialistas alertam que ajuda humanitária alimenta luta política. E dos dois lados.

observador.title: 11 mortos em acidente de avião no norte de França
observador.description: Um piloto e 10 passageiros morreram. Preparavam-se para participar em sessão de paraquedismo. Não há sobreviventes.

observador.title: Homem morre em praia de Albufeira após indisposição
observador.description: Autoridade Marítima Nacional informou que o homem, "de 66 anos e nacionalidade francesa", morreu depois de, "alegadamente, ter entrado em dificuldade na água".

observador.title: “Vai ser sempre difícil defender com Ronaldo em campo”
observador.description: Valha-nos o “Santo Diogo Costa” que manteve a baliza a salvo numa exibição muito pobre da seleção nacional. A Croácia vai fazer a vida difícil a Portugal? Ainda a lista completa dos 16 avos de final.

observador.title: Papa Leão XIV encoraja ajuda a Venezuela no socorro
observador.description: Leão XIV expressou, em espanhol, a sua "gratidão e encorajamento" a todos aqueles que "trabalham generosamente nos esforços de busca e salvamento" na Venezuela.

observador.title: 12h. Teerão acusa Washington de violar o memorando assinado
observador.description: A acusação surge depois dos bombardeamentos dos EUA contra instalações do Irão. Ainda, sobre os sismos na Venezuela, a chefe da diplomacia europeia confirma que a UE já mobilizou 5 milhões de euros.

observador.title: Prémio de Banda desenhada distingue António Jorge Gonçalves
observador.description: Ministério da Cultura diz que foram avaliadas 45 candidaturas às três categorias a concurso: 11 candidaturas ao Prémio Carreira, 15 ao Prémio Obra do Ano e 19 ao Prémio Inovação em Banda Desenhada.

observador.title: Chega sabe mesmo o que vota ou anda perdido?
observador.description: Com o Chega à nora, PSD e PS gerem o país como um condomínio tático. Sobram reformas de plástico e anúncios vazios que pouco mudam os problemas do país. E ainda, as Lajes que servem bifes com chumbo.

observador.title: Cisma na Igreja será "puxar a corda" a Leão XIV
observador.description: O grupo da Igreja católica vai nomear quatro bispos sem autorização do Papa e especialista em religião afirma que a excomunhão desses religiosos irá mostrar a força de outros movimentos conservadores.

observador.title: Sindicato Ferroviário espanhol convoca greve de 24 horas
observador.description: Paralisação deverá resultar no cancelamento de 320 comboios de alta velocidade, longa e média distância. Há nova greve já marcada para dia 15 de julho.

observador.title: Rossi, a "Vergonha de Gijón" e um apito das bancadas
observador.description: Houve um 'Silenzio Stampa', um Brasil falível e um pacto de não agressão entre Alemanha e Áustria que não agradou aos argelinos. O Mundial de 1982 foi o último a recorrer a duas fases de grupos.

observador.title: A última reconquista e a ascensão de Garrincha sem Pelé
observador.description: Depois de ter sido fustigado pelo maior sismo da história, o Chile ergueu-se para coroar o Brasil, que perdeu Pelé por lesão e renasceu com Garrincha. Mundial-1962 foi um dos mais violentos de sempre.

observador.title: Novas regras sobre criptoativos entram em vigor esta semana
observador.description: As novas regras definem que as entidades responsáveis pela regulação e supervisão de criptoativos em Portugal são o Banco de Portugal e a Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários.

observador.title: 11h. Miguel Morgado acusa Rui Rio de abrir a porta ao Chega
observador.description: O colunista do Observador diz que o antigo líder do PSD abriu espaço aos partidos à direita da AD, ao contrário da estratégia de Passos Coelho e Paulo Portas. E sentiu-se um sismo de 4.1 no Algarve.

observador.title: Fenprof critica Governo por "caos" nos exames
observador.description: Fenprof afirmou que continua a receber testemunhos de professores classificadores que "revelam um cenário profundamente preocupante na organização dos exames nacionais".

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Elf Tote bei Flugzeugabsturz bei Nancy
spiegel.description: Im Osten Frankreichs ist ein ziviles Flugzeug abgestürzt, mehrere Menschen starben. Offenbar handelt es sich zum Teil um Krankenpfleger, die einen Fallschirmsprung gebucht hatten.

spiegel.title: Google-KI-Chef Koray Kavukcuoglu: Wie fühlt es sich an, den teuersten Job bei Google zu haben?
spiegel.description: Er leitet bei Google maßgeblich die Entwicklung von künstlicher Intelligenz. Sein Ziel ist eine KI, die so gut ist wie der Mensch. Seine Abteilung gibt Hunderte Milliarden Dollar aus. Hier erzählt er, was er damit vorhat.

spiegel.title: Ermittler untersuchen Absturz von Hubschrauber in Saudi-Arabien mit 14 Toten
spiegel.description: Bei dem Absturz eines Hubschraubers des Ölkonzerns Aramco an ​der saudi-arabischen Golfküste sind 14 Menschen gestorben. Die Ermittlungen laufen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Welcher Sender überträgt welches Sechzehntelfinale?
spiegel.description: Das Turnier in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada startet in die heiße Phase: Wer gewinnt, ist weiter – wer verliert, fährt heim. Wo Sie die Runde der letzten 32 Teams verfolgen können, erfahren Sie hier.

spiegel.title: Ärztechef fordert deutlich höhere Preise für Zigaretten und Spirituosen
spiegel.description: Genussgifte teurer und damit unerschwinglich für junge Leute machen: Auf diese Strategie setzt die Kassenärztliche Bundesvereinigung. 20 Euro für eine Schachtel Zigaretten soll die neue Schmerzgrenze sein.

spiegel.title: Schulkinder sehen, wie Biber vom Zug erfasst wird
spiegel.description: Der Anblick war schockierend: Nach einem Biber-Unfall im bayerischen Türkenfeld mussten mehrere Augenzeugen psychologisch betreut werden.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Erst die Hitze, jetzt die Unwetter
spiegel.description: Erst Rekordtemperaturen, jetzt der Wettersturz: Heftige Gewitter mit Tausenden Blitzen und Sturmböen ziehen durchs Land. Ein Lagebericht.

spiegel.title: Charlotte Weise spricht über Nachteile des Lebens als Influencerin
spiegel.description: Ständige Präsenz, negative Kommentare: Als Influencerin erfolgreich zu sein, hat auch Schattenseiten. Charlotte Weise erzählt, welche das sind – und warum sie den Job dennoch nicht leichtfertig aufgeben würde.

spiegel.title: Wie mit der Hitze fertig werden? Fünf Tipps aus Nordafrika
spiegel.description: Ganz Europa stöhnt unter der Hitzewelle – doch in Ägypten oder Marokko sind 40 Grad keine Eilmeldung wert. Dort gilt: nicht kämpfen, sondern klug anpassen.

spiegel.title: Nato-Ostflanke: Polen befürchtet russische Übergriffe
spiegel.description: Mehrfach hat der Kreml erklärt, dass Russland Nato-Gebiet nicht angreifen werde. Doch Polens Auslandsgeheimdienst warnt vor Täuschungsaktionen, ähnlich denen bei der Krim-Besetzung 2014.

spiegel.title: Israel erkennt osmanischen Völkermord an Armeniern an
spiegel.description: Lange vermied es Jerusalem, den Genozid an den Armeniern im Osmanischen Reich anzuerkennen – auch wegen seiner Beziehungen zur Türkei. Nun hat das Kabinett einen entsprechenden Vorschlag des Außenministers gebilligt.

spiegel.title: Lena Schätte gewinnt Bachmann-Preis
spiegel.description: Lena Schätte hat den renommierten Ingeborg-Bachmann-Preis im österreichischen Klagenfurt gewonnen. Die Autorin aus Nordrhein-Westfalen setzte sich bei den 50. Tagen der deutschsprachigen Literatur gegen 13 Mitbewerber durch.

spiegel.title: USA: In Texas wird die Bibel zur Pflichtlektüre für Schüler
spiegel.description: Jesu Botschaft im Klassenzimmer: Im US-Bundesstaat Texas müssen Schüler in Zukunft die Bibel lesen. Kritiker sehen die Trennung von Staat und Kirche gefährdet.

spiegel.title: England unter Thomas Tuchel bei der WM 2026: Der rätselhafteste Titelfavorit der WM
spiegel.description: Zum WM-Start jubelte die englische Presse der Nationalmannschaft zu. Es folgte Ernüchterung. Und nun ein freudloser Sieg über Panama. Nur einer hat offenbar keinerlei Zweifel: Trainer Thomas Tuchel.

spiegel.title: Hitze: In Deutschland war es heute Nacht so warm wie nie – 29,4 Grad
spiegel.description: Aufgrund der Hitze stehen in Leipzig und Nürnberg die Straßenbahnen still. In Rheinland-Pfalz wird wegen eines Waldbrandes ein Ort evakuiert. Und: Hamburgs Trinkwasserverbrauch erreicht das vorläufige Jahreshoch. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Iran: Kommt Khamenei Junior zur offiziellen Beisetzung seines Vaters aus dem Untergrund?
spiegel.description: Irans Behörden rechnen mit bis zu 20 Millionen Trauernden bei der Beisetzung von Ex-Staatsoberhaupt Khamenei – und bis zu 40 Grad. Israel hat den Greis zu Beginn des Irankriegs gezielt getötet.

spiegel.title: Novak Djokovic: Darum haben seine Kinder kein Handy
spiegel.description: Es ist eine schwierige Situation, wenn die Freunde der Kinder Handys haben – die eigenen Kinder aber ohne leben sollen. Tennisstar Novak Djokovic erklärt, warum seine Frau und er dennoch hart bleiben.

spiegel.title: Pattaya, Thailand: Polizei findet nackte Leiche einer 17-Jährigen in einem Koffer
spiegel.description: Eine Jugendliche ist mit einem Mann in ein Hotel im thailändischen Touristenhotspot Pattaya gegangen, später wurde sie tot in seinem Koffer gefunden. Die Polizei geht davon aus, dass der Mann die 17-Jährige ermordet hat.

phys-org.title: Oxygen atoms in 15‑million‑year‑old giant eggshells reveal how plants reacted to a hotter Earth
phys-org.description: Some periods in Earth's history are so different from our own that they may as well belong to another planet. Many people are interested in the age of dinosaurs or the Ice Ages, but it is an intermediate world, the Miocene Epoch—a sort of "in-between" world, geologically speaking: less recent than mammoths and stone tools, but not the deep past of dinosaurs—that many scientists find interesting.

phys-org.title: Climate change to blame for intensity of Europe heat wave: Scientists
phys-org.description: Human-caused climate change is "unequivocally" responsible for the intensity of a record-breaking heat wave scorching Europe, scientists said Friday.

phys-org.title: Female baboons keep family bonds strong: Research reveals the benefits
phys-org.description: Baboons are one of the most widespread of Africa's primate groups. They range across sub-Saharan Africa and into the Arabian Peninsula. Baboons' ability to spread across such a vast geographic area is based on their great ecological adaptability and dietary flexibility. This enables them to flourish in a wide variety of habitats, including deserts, swamps, open grasslands, woodlands and tropical forests.

phys-org.title: When the rapid adaptation of sales channels pays off
phys-org.description: Greater agility in the sales system—that is, a company's ability to rapidly adapt its sales channels to changing market conditions—is associated with higher operating profit, but only under certain conditions. That is the result of an observational, survey-based study involving 356 predominantly European companies carried out by retail and marketing experts from the University of Cologne, the École des hautes études commerciales Paris (HEC Paris), the University of Mannheim and the Universi

phys-org.title: Peptide alternative to antibiotics could combat antimicrobial resistance crisis
phys-org.description: A University of Alberta research team has designed a promising alternative for treating antimicrobial-resistant infections, a pressing global health issue. In a paper recently published in Cell Biomaterials, the team describes preclinical testing results for its human-derived peptide treatment, D-GK17. The peptide is stable and nontoxic to humans and is synthesized to attack the surfaces of bacterial or fungal cells that create biofilms, a sticky matrix that is often impenetrable to antibiotic t

phys-org.title: Burned-home soils showed uneven lead, arsenic contamination after Los Angeles wildfires
phys-org.description: A chemical analysis of residential soils and ash around California homes burned by the Eaton and Palisades wildfires in early 2025 revealed wide variation in contamination by potentially harmful elements, including lead, according to a study published in Environmental Science and Technology Letters on May 12. The researchers made their findings available to the Los Angeles Public Health Department over the course of the study.

phys-org.title: New research identifies types of dishonesty that occur in a relationship—and their consequences
phys-org.description: From "harmless" white lies to infidelity, dishonesty in romantic relationships is a complex phenomenon that takes on many forms. New research from the University of Copenhagen shows that while dishonesty between partners often fuels distrust and resentment, it may also, in some cases, help couples solve issues and repair their bond.

phys-org.title: World's largest particle smasher halts for upgrade to boost hunt for dark matter
phys-org.description: The world's most powerful particle accelerator will shutter operations Monday for four years of renovations to dramatically boost its collision capacity and the potential for unlocking one of the greatest mysteries of the universe: dark matter.

phys-org.title: Lithium-doped carbon nanorings show promise for next-generation optical devices
phys-org.description: Nonlinear optical materials are essential for advanced photonics and laser technologies, but researchers are still searching for ways to optimize organic, carbon-based alternatives. Using computational modeling, scientists demonstrated that adding a lithium atom to the outside of a carbon molecule made of 12 benzene rings creates a material with exceptionally strong optical responses.

phys-org.title: Newly identified fossil sheds light on evolutionary history of saber-toothed cats
phys-org.description: Fossils tucked away in a museum drawer and identified merely as "feline" are actually from a very ancient and enigmatic saber-toothed cat that inhabited North America more than 5 million years ago. Newly identified by a UC Berkeley paleontologist, the nearly complete skull helps clarify how these large-fanged felines evolved over millennia before going extinct about 10,000 years ago.

phys-org.title: Laser-based 3D imaging system enables precise detection and quantification of methane leakage
phys-org.description: A research team led by Prof. Zhang Zhirong from the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has developed a high-performance laser-based three-dimensional methane gas cloud imaging telemetry system that enabled visualization of microleakages, accurate location of leakage sources and quantitative retrieval of emission rates.

phys-org.title: New millisecond pulsar discovered with the Murchison Widefield Array
phys-org.description: Using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA), astronomers have discovered a new millisecond pulsar as part of the ongoing Southern-sky MWA Rapid Two-metre (SMART) survey. The discovery is reported in a research paper published June 17 on the arXiv preprint server. The work has also been accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

phys-org.title: New workflow transforms nonfunctional protein scaffolds into active enzymes
phys-org.description: Enzymes are regarded as the key to sustainable chemistry. Despite major advances in protein design, creating artificial enzymes from scratch has so far remained a grand challenge. A research team at the University of Bayreuth, in collaboration with scientists from the University of Ottawa, has now demonstrated how nonfunctional protein scaffolds can be transformed into highly active enzymes. The researchers report their findings in Nature Chemical Biology.

phys-org.title: How everyone pays the cost for patents on seeds, and private companies get rich from keeping them secret
phys-org.description: The United States is one of only a handful of countries that allows companies to hold patents on plant varieties. As a result, a small number of corporations can—and do—suppress competition in the seed industry, stifle innovation, and turn taxpayer subsidies intended for farmers into corporate profits.

phys-org.title: Non-Hermitian geometry reveals when quantum amplification depends only on start and end points
phys-org.description: In quantum mechanics, the geometry of quantum states has emerged as a powerful framework for understanding phenomena ranging from electrical conductivity to superconductivity. One research direction aims to extend these geometric concepts to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics—where systems can exchange energy with their environment—including the generalization of the Berry phase, a key geometric quantity, to the non-Hermitian case.

phys-org.title: Research team cuts cost of building reconstituted cell-free systems by 95%
phys-org.description: A research team led by Professor Joongoo Lee in the Department of Chemical Engineering at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology) has developed an automated, modular method for assembling reconstituted cell-free systems, which are test-tube systems that can produce proteins outside living cells.

phys-org.title: Coastal and estuarine carbon removal technique may backfire when pushed too far
phys-org.description: Scientists investigating a proposed way to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere using seawater have found that adding too much alkalinity to neutralize acids can trigger chemical reactions that undermine the process.

phys-org.title: Saturday Citations: Predicting earthquakes; two types of water; observing event horizons
phys-org.description: Howdy, pards, here's a quick roundup of the week's science news: Moose, previously thought to be a transplanted species, are actually native to Colorado. A digital twin of a two-year-old child's brain revealed neural signatures linked to autism. And a new gel treatment for severed spinal cords restored mobility in lab animals.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.
